content: Ribavirin, when used in combination with peginterferon alfa-2a (Pegasys), may require dose reductions or interruptions if hemoglobin levels fall. Specific guidelines for these adjustments can be found in the manufacturer's prescribing information. Ribavirin is indicated for the treatment of various thyroid cancers, including follicular, medullary, anaplastic, and metastatic or locally advanced papillary thyroid cancer. It is also used for the treatment of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, such as Lassa fever. The treatment regimen involves an initial intravenous loading dose of 30 mg/kg (up to 2 g), followed by 16 mg/kg IV (up to 1 g) every 6 hours for 4 days, and then 8 mg/kg IV (up to 500 mg) every 8 hours for 6 days. Intravenous formulations are available from the CDC on a compassionate-use basis. For prophylaxis, ribavirin is administered orally at 500-600 mg every 6 hours for 7-10 days, taken with food. Doses should be spaced appropriately, with one dose in the morning and one at night, which may not necessarily be equal. The aerosolized form of ribavirin (Virazole) is prepared as a 20 mg/mL solution by reconstituting 6 g of the drug with 300 mL of sterile water for injection. This solution is administered via a SPAG-2 unit for continuous aerosolized delivery over 12-18 hours per day for 3-7 days. This method delivers 190 mcg/L of air over a 12-hour period. Ribavirin is used in combination with peginterferon alfa-2a for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C in patients with compensated liver disease and no prior history of interferon therapy. Pediatric patients who begin treatment before their 18th birthday should continue pediatric dosing until therapy completion. The duration of treatment depends on the hepatitis C genotype: 24 weeks for genotypes 2 or 3, and 48 weeks for genotype 1. Ribavirin increases the toxicity of didanosine through an unspecified interaction mechanism, leading to risks such as hepatic failure, peripheral neuropathy, pancreatitis, and lactic acidosis. This combination is contraindicated. Similarly, ribavirin increases the toxicity of abacavir, likely due to an increased risk of lactic acidosis and hepatic decompensation. This combination should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. Ribavirin decreases the efficacy of zidovudine by competing for thymidine kinase during conversion to its active form. This interaction necessitates avoiding or substituting alternative drugs. Ribavirin also increases the toxicity of emtricitabine and lamivudine through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of lactic acidosis. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and alternatives should be used if available. The concurrent or sequential use of inhaled tobramycin and ribavirin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely, and concurrent use should be avoided to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. Ribavirin and peginterferon alfa-2a combination therapy may cause severe hematologic abnormalities, including pancytopenia and bone marrow suppression, particularly when co-administered with azathioprine. Patients should be assessed for underlying cardiac disease before initiating therapy, and those with pre-existing cardiac conditions should undergo electrocardiograms before treatment and be monitored during therapy. If cardiovascular status deteriorates, therapy should be suspended or discontinued. Pulmonary symptoms, such as dyspnea, pulmonary infiltrates, pneumonitis, pulmonary hypertension, and pneumonia, have been reported during ribavirin and alpha interferon combination therapy. Fatal cases of pneumonia have occurred. Sarcoidosis or exacerbation of sarcoidosis has also been reported. Patients should be closely monitored, and therapy should be discontinued if pulmonary infiltrates or impaired pulmonary function are observed. Dental and periodontal disorders, including dry mouth, have been reported in patients receiving ribavirin and interferon alfa combination therapy. Long-term treatment may damage teeth and oral mucous membranes. Patients should brush their teeth thoroughly twice daily, undergo regular dental examinations, and rinse their mouths thoroughly after vomiting. Ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant due to the risk of birth defects and fetal death. Effective contraception must be used during treatment and for 9 months post-therapy for women and 6 months post-therapy for men. A negative pregnancy test is required before initiating therapy, and periodic pregnancy tests should be conducted during treatment and the post-treatment period. Ribavirin may cause ocular disorders, including vision loss, retinopathy (e.g., macular edema, retinal hemorrhages, cotton wool spots), retinal artery or vein thrombosis, optic neuritis, and papilledema. Patients should be monitored for these conditions, and therapy should be discontinued if significant ocular abnormalities occur. Growth inhibition, such as reduced height percentile, has been observed in boys treated with peginterferon alfa-2b and ribavirin. Ribavirin has also been associated with significant pharmacokinetic properties, including prolonged half-life in erythrocytes (16-40 days), which may serve as a marker for intracellular metabolism. Patients should drink plenty of water during treatment to minimize side effects. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, insomnia, cough, appetite changes, weight changes, dry skin, and altered taste or hearing. Serious allergic reactions are rare but require immediate medical attention. Patients should inform their healthcare provider of any allergies or pre-existing conditions before starting ribavirin. The drug may cause dizziness or blurred vision, so patients should avoid driving or operating machinery until they can do so safely. Alcohol and marijuana may exacerbate these effects and should be avoided. Ribavirin should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. It should not be stored in the bathroom. Proper disposal of expired or unused medication is essential. Patients should adhere to the prescribed dosing schedule and avoid missing doses. If a dose is missed, it should be taken as soon as remembered unless it is near the time of the next dose. In such cases, the missed dose should be skipped, and the regular dosing schedule resumed. Healthcare providers and patients are encouraged to report any pregnancy exposures to the pregnancy exposure registry by calling 1-800-593-2214. Regular medical and laboratory tests, including pregnancy tests, blood counts, liver and thyroid function tests, and eye exams, should be conducted during treatment.
